name: Asturian gaita (Iberian Celtic bagpipe)
lineage: Asturian gaita Iberian Celtic-bagpipe tradition of Asturias (northern Spain), the canonical Asturian regional-folk-music instrumental signature. The gaita asturiana is a mouth-blown single-drone bagpipe distinct from the larger Galician gaita gallega and the Scottish Highland pipes in tuning and ornament-vocabulary. Performance: solo gaita or gaita-and-tambor (drum-pair) accompanying voice, dance, or solo instrumental display. Repertoire spans foliada wedding-celebration repertoire, vaqueirada cattle-herder dance-music, and the canonical Asturian-Celtic revival-period compositions of the late-twentieth century. Distinguished from Galician gaita gallega by Asturian-specific tuning and ornamental conventions. The Asturian Cultural Council and the parallel Galician Real Academia de la Gaita anchor institutional preservation.
